subject.title: Control-plane hardening from Optimus ops findings

question: After the blocking storage, redaction, counting, rebase, and proof fixes, should OpenClaw adopt the diagnose JSON plus persistent diagnostic-state contracts as one core operator surface, or require them to land as separate focused PRs?
rationale: The permanent schema, persistence, and security ownership are product and compatibility choices that automation cannot safely approve, and the current combined branch is too broad to infer maintainer intent.

options.title: Require focused PRs
options.body: Split SQLite diagnostic storage, diagnose JSON/redaction, plugin contract validation, and handoff metadata into current-main-based PRs with independent proof.

options.title: Sponsor the combined contract
options.body: Keep one PR only if an owner explicitly accepts the combined operator API and reviews the rebased exact merge result.

options.title: Pause the project stack
options.body: Close or defer the branch if the combined control-plane surface is not a current core priority.

recommendation.title: Require focused PRs
recommendation.body: Split SQLite diagnostic storage, diagnose JSON/redaction, plugin contract validation, and handoff metadata into current-main-based PRs with independent proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin, Codex, doctor, and architecture history makes this the strongest available owner for the permanent core/operator boundary decision.
